title: Prior KSATEXM and near-saturation research reuse map
purpose: Reuse prior SWAP 4.3.1 hydraulic and performance research as diagnostic evidence, stress-case design and candidate-closure context for RossFast without promoting earlier results into current Ross qualification gates.
reuse_rules: Prior project evidence may define stress materials, probe locations, constitutive diagnostics and candidate hypotheses.
Prior project evidence does not by itself qualify RossFast, C2A, a new conductivity closure, saturation crossing, groundwater coupling or FullRichards equivalence.
Exact SWAP 4.3.1 KSATEXM remains Class A source-bound physics and must retain its own fail-closed qualification lineage.

Any Schaap-van-Genuchten-inspired or otherwise modified near-saturation relation is Class B physical hydraulics and must be implemented identically in FullRichards and RossFast before solver-comparison claims.
Performance pathologies caused by a Jacobian or boundary inconsistency are evidence about numerical sensitivity, not evidence that the constitutive law itself is wrong.

facts.observed_solver_effect: dry O05 required about 11-14 percent more Newton work than O02 with the same accepted-step count; normal Hupsel O05 was not uniformly slower

ross_reuse: retain O05 as a mandatory wet-end stress material
place dense constitutive and face-response probes around the narrow KSATEXM transition interval
track K, dK/dh where defined, MFP slope, face mobility and table interpolation error in addition to flux error
use the observed tiny theta interval as evidence that theta-only uniform tabulation may be poorly conditioned without a physics-aligned coordinate

prior_project_strands.interpretation: The near-saturation KSATEXM regime can amplify an inconsistent surface/ponding Jacobian dramatically. This does not prove KSATEXM physics invalid. It proves that near-saturation qualification must separate constitutive conditioning from boundary/Jacobian correctness.
ross_reuse: add near-ponding and saturation-approach cases to later timestep/boundary qualification
require structural separation between constitutive face-response error and boundary-contract error
use bounded-cost behavior as an explicit metric once RossFast reaches transient qualification

reusable_methods: compare analytic or candidate C(h) with independent numerical dtheta/dh
compare candidate dK/dh with independent numerical derivative of the actual K(h)
test inverse consistency h -> theta -> h
treat piecewise joins and practically saturated limits explicitly rather than hiding them in generic finite-difference probes
keep constitutive evaluation and solver-state timing explicit so caches cannot become order-dependent
prior_project_strands.ross_reuse: Use this test philosophy as the constitutive pre-gate for both Class A KSATEXM representation and any Class B near-saturation closure.

facts: CofGen(25:42) are derived hydraulic data, not independent physical state
near-saturation and air-entry derived terms include CofGen(26:28) and polynomial extension constants CofGen(41:42)
derived constitutive data must be refreshed after accepted primary hydraulic parameter changes and should be versioned in the target architecture
ross_reuse: Ross lookup tables and closure coefficients must be immutable/versioned derived parameter payloads keyed to the hydraulic parameter/closure identity
no face table belongs in persistent per-column physical state
tillage or other accepted hydraulic parameter mutation must invalidate/rebind derived Ross constitutive payloads explicitly

facts: The project material reports that the standard Van Genuchten conductivity shape can be too steep near saturation for heavy soils and does not represent air-entry/macropore behavior well.

The NHI/MetaSWAP line uses a simplified application inspired by Schaap and van Genuchten (2006) to modify the near-saturation k-h relation, implemented through table-based soil hydraulics in SWAP/MetaSWAP contexts.
The project material reports substantial hydrologic sensitivity to that near-saturation k-h modification in heavy-clay examples.

primary_literature.citation: Schaap MG, van Genuchten MT (2006), A Modified Mualem-van Genuchten Formulation for Improved Description of the Hydraulic Conductivity Near Saturation, Vadose Zone Journal 5:27-34
source_level_findings: introduces a small non-zero air-entry pressure; reported optimum about -4 cm in the analysed database
uses a pressure-dependent piecewise linear conductivity correction between 0 and -40 cm
reports a stronger correction from 0 to -4 cm and a smaller correction from -4 to -40 cm
authors explicitly describe the correction as empirical and advise caution because near-saturated K measurements are uncertain

ross_reuse: promote this line to the first literature-backed Class B candidate family rather than inventing an arbitrary smoothing polynomial
keep the NHI simplified implementation distinct from the exact 2006 formulation until its equations and parameter mapping are source-bound
test whether an air-entry-aware closure improves Ross table compactness, MFP smoothness and transient bounded-cost behavior while preserving mass conservation

current_ross_context.interpretation: Repeated failure of increasingly physics-aligned table coordinates strengthens the case for reusing the earlier KSATEXM stress evidence and separately investigating a literature-backed Class B closure, but does not justify altering Class A acceptance criteria or rewriting KSATEXM.

recommended_research_sequence: Persist the exact R2 failure metrics and fail-close that representation before opening another Class A redesign.
Reconstruct the earlier O05 and N4 probes as frozen reusable ROSS01 stress fixtures with explicit provenance.
Source-bind the exact NHI simplified Schaap-van-Genuchten implementation if available; otherwise reconstruct the 2006 MMVG equations independently and keep the NHI variant labelled unresolved.

Define one Class B candidate contract before running it: same theta(h) policy, K(h) equations, air-entry parameter, saturated endpoint, continuity class, MFP definition, allowed materials and immutable parameter identity.

Run constitutive qualification first, then steady-face qualification, then FullRichards same-physics transient reference tests. Only after those pass should RossFast transient or groundwater qualification use the Class B variant.
